findings.summary: The repeated decode check is redundant after the validator rejects every percent sign.
findings.consequence: This keeps an extra validation branch, constants, and test expectations in the route-param boundary even though the later `%` rejection already rejects malformed, singly encoded, and multiply encoded values before any caller can use them.
findings.evidence: In the owned unit, line 150 decodes the route param and line 151 requires the decoded value to equal the original, but line 155 rejects all values containing `%`. The listed tests for `%`, `%ZZ`, `%25`, `%2e%2e`, and `%252e%252e` would still fail validation through line 155. Direct callers pass Nuxt route params or backend author identities onward only after this boolean guard, and `authorProfilePath` performs encoding for output paths.
findings.recommendation: Remove the `repeatedlyDecode(value, maxAuthorIdLength)` check from `validateAuthorRouteParam` and let the existing scalar, slash, backslash, control, surrogate, percent, and dot-segment checks define the boundary. Keep `repeatedlyDecode` for the href sanitizers where percent decoding is still semantically required.
